title: Conjecture 2.2
statement_text: There is a polynomial $P$ such that every graph $G$ that contains no prism, pyramid, theta or turtle has at most $P(|V(G)|)$ minimal separators.
context_text: Graphs are finite and simple; $G$ contains $H$ if some induced subgraph of $G$ is isomorphic to $H$, and $G$ is $H$-free otherwise; paths are chordless. A hole is an induced cycle on at least $4$ vertices (a square is a hole of length $4$), and a graph is even-hole-free if it has no hole with an even number of vertices. A theta consists of three internally disjoint chordless paths of length at least $2$ between two vertices $a,b$, with no edges between the paths except at $a$ and $b$; a pyramid consists of three chordless paths $a\dots b_1$, $a\dots b_2$, $a\dots b_3$ of length at least $1$, two of length at least $2$, disjoint except at $a$, such that $b_1b_2b_3$ is a triangle and there are no other edges between the paths; a prism consists of three disjoint chordless paths $a_i\dots b_i$ ($i=1,2,3$) of length at least $1$ such that $a_1a_2a_3$ and $b_1b_2b_3$ are triangles and there are no other edges between the paths. A wheel is a hole (the rim) plus a vertex (the center) with at least three neighbours on it; it is an even wheel if the center has an even number of neighbours on the rim. A turtle consists of two internally disjoint chordless $u$–$v$ paths $P_1,P_2$ forming a hole, plus two adjacent vertices $x,y$ outside them such that $x$ has at least three neighbours in $P_1$ and none in $P_2$, and $y$ at least three neighbours in $P_2$ and none in $P_1$. A set $C\subseteq V(G)$ is a minimal separator if it is a minimal set separating some pair of vertices $a,b$ (equivalently, $G\setminus C$ has two components $L,R$ such that every vertex of $C$ has neighbours in both). By results of Bouchitté and Todinca, a polynomial bound on the number of minimal separators in a class gives a polynomial-time algorithm for maximum weight independent set on that class. The $k$-prisms (two $k$-cliques joined by a perfect matching), their variants the $k$-pyramids and $k$-thetas, and the $k$-turtles have exponentially many minimal separators and contain respectively a prism, pyramid, theta and turtle; since the authors could not imagine other examples with exponentially many minimal separators, they propose this conjecture as in some sense the best possible statement. The authors prove that every (square, prism, pyramid, theta, even wheel)-free graph on $n$ vertices has $O(n^8)$ minimal separators (enumerable in $O(n^{10})$ time); this class contains all (even hole, pyramid)-free graphs, so maximum weight independent set is polynomial-time solvable on (even hole, pyramid)-free graphs. Every prism, theta and turtle contains an even hole (turtles contain even wheels), so restricting the conjecture to (prism, pyramid, theta, even wheel)-free graphs gives a weakening, which the authors could only prove after also excluding squares.
paper_title: Maximum independent sets in (pyramid, even hole)-free graphs

title: Open problem: MIS complexity in even-hole-free graphs
statement_text: The complexity of computing a maximum independent set in an even-hole-free graph is not known; that is, can a maximum independent set be computed in polynomial time in even-hole-free graphs (graphs with no induced cycle of even length at least $4$)?
context_text: Graphs are finite and simple; $G$ contains $H$ if some induced subgraph of $G$ is isomorphic to $H$, and $G$ is $H$-free otherwise; paths are chordless. A hole is an induced cycle on at least $4$ vertices (a square is a hole of length $4$), and a graph is even-hole-free if it has no hole with an even number of vertices. Even-hole-free graphs have been the object of much research (see Vušković's survey), but this question is open. The paper gives a polynomial-time algorithm for maximum weight independent set on (even hole, pyramid)-free graphs, where a pyramid consists of three chordless paths $a\dots b_1$, $a\dots b_2$, $a\dots b_3$ of length at least $1$, two of length at least $2$, disjoint except at $a$, such that $b_1b_2b_3$ is a triangle and there are no other edges between the paths. The method is a decomposition theorem plus a polynomial bound ($O(n^8)$) on the number of minimal separators, which yields the algorithm via results of Bouchitté and Todinca; the bound holds more generally for (square, prism, pyramid, theta, even wheel)-free graphs. The authors hope that the pyramid-free case may help to understand the whole class, since the presence of a pyramid strongly restricts the structure of an even-hole-free graph.
notes: Stated as a known open problem in the field (referencing a survey [10]); no specific attribution to individual authors is given in the text.
paper_title: Maximum independent sets in (pyramid, even hole)-free graphs

title: Open problem: polynomial separator property for (prism, pyramid, theta, even wheel)-free graphs
statement_text: Do (prism, pyramid, theta, even wheel)-free graphs have polynomially many minimal separators, i.e. is there $b$ such that every such graph $G$ has at most $|V(G)|^b$ minimal separators? The authors were not able to prove it.
context_text: Graphs are finite and simple; $G$ contains $H$ if some induced subgraph of $G$ is isomorphic to $H$, and $G$ is $H$-free otherwise; paths are chordless.
